The following text was generated by one of these five AI language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

All five options are AI-generated - do not consider the possibility that a human wrote it. Read the text carefully and identify which model most likely produced it, based on writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- TEXT ---
Learning to budget your money each month is worth the effort because it gives you control instead of leaving you guessing. When you know how much money is coming in and where it needs to go, you are much less likely to spend more than you earn. A budget helps you see the difference between what you need, what you want, and what you can actually afford, so you do not end up relying on credit cards, overdrafts, or loans just to get through the month.

It also helps you build savings over time, even if you can only set aside a small amount at first. Without a budget, extra money can disappear on small purchases before you realize it. With a budget, you can make saving part of your plan instead of something you only do if money happens to be left over. Over months and years, those regular savings can become an emergency fund, a vacation fund, or money for bigger goals that would otherwise feel impossible.

Most importantly, budgeting can reduce financial stress. Money feels a lot less overwhelming when you have a clear plan for bills, spending, savings, and unexpected expenses. You may not always have as much money as you want, but knowing where it is going makes life feel more manageable. A budget is not about restricting yourself forever; it is about giving yourself more confidence, fewer surprises, and better choices.
--- END ---
Output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
